newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ALL-STAR GUARD REGGIE MILLER RE-SIGNS WITH PACERS. [CORRECTED 04:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ALL-STAR GUARD REGGIE MILLER RE-SIGNS WITH PACERS. [CORRECTED 04:22 GMT]

text.p: All-Star guard Reggie Miller has signed a long-term contract to stay with the Indiana Pacers, the team announced Monday.

No terms were disclosed, but the ESPN sports television network reported that the deal is for $36 million over four years. Miller was the last unsigned star in the NBA's biggest offseason of free-agent signings ever.

The deal probably will keep the 31-year-old Miller in Indiana for the remainder of his career and was reached the same day the club began training camp in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Pacers general manager Donnie Walsh had set the beginning of training camp to get the deal done.
"Obviously, I'm happy," Pacers coach Larry Brown said. "I think the commitment the (team owners) Simons made, and the job Donnie has done getting this done is really a positive."

Miller averaged 21.1 points per game last season, his ninth in the NBA. He suffered a fractured right orbit bone late in the season and missed four playoff games before returning for the decisive fifth game of Indiana's first-round series against the Atlanta Hawks.
Wearing protective glasses, Miller scored 16 of his 29 points in the fourth quarter, but Indiana was eliminated with an 89-87 loss.

Miller is one of the best outside shooters in the game. He has averaged better than 19.6 points in each of the last seven seasons and has 1,203 three-pointers, second on the all-time list to Dale Ellis. (Corrects from "tops on the all-time list")
The Pacers reached the seventh game of the Eastern Conference finals in 1994 and 1995.
"I'm also happy for Reggie," Brown added. "He's respected and loved here and it's good to know he will get to retire here in Indianapolis."
Miller made NBA All-Star teams in 1990, 1995 and 1996 and was a member of Dream Team III, which won the gold medal at the Summer Olympics in Atlanta.
The re-signing of Miller keeps the nucleus of the Pacers intact. Earlier this year, they re-signed free agent forwards Antonio Davis and Dale Davis to long-term deals.
